steps.note: Preview the citation: `add` with `--dry-run` prints the diff and writes nothing.
Write it: drop `--dry-run`; the report says it added fetch-timeout to frontmatter.
Check it: both ends current, and the summary reads 0 findings.
When the source changes: the check reports `changed since <commit>, 1 commit`, an error.
`--show-diff` puts the commit subject and the diff on screen.
A plain `update` won't touch a changed source, says so, and exits 1.
After fixing the sentence, `update --accept` re-pins both ends at HEAD.
When the source moves: the check finds the line at its new number, a warning, exit 0.
When the page changes: an inserted paragraph moves the claim, a notice.
`update` rewrites `claim.lines` as it rewrites the source's.
Edit the sentence: claim-changed, a warning.
Accept the edited claim with `update --accept --only fetch-timeout`.
Anchor with a marker: `--marker` writes the marker and pins what it anchors.
Pin a code block with `--quote`; `add` checks the block reproduces the cited lines.
All three citations show up in one check with 0 findings.

scaffolding: lib/limits.ts and docs/limits.md hold the page's example source and page; manni.config.yaml declares the docs-pages collection over docs/**/*.md so a bare `manni cite check` reads docs/limits.md.

The workspace is the starting state: no citations yet. The page has the reader (or someone) change the source, commit it, move it, and edit the page, so a spec makes those edits and the source commit itself (`changed since <commit>, 1 commit` and the --show-diff subject need that commit in history).
